items.title: New Research — LeVJEPA: Efficient & Scalable Video Pretraining without the Heuristics
items.summary: LeVJEPA shows that high-quality video representations can be learned with a radically simpler JEPA-style system — one encoder, one objective, and no target network, predictor, or stop-gradient — while matching or beating V-JEPA 2 with as much as 20.8× less pretraining compute and producing causal representations suited to future world models

items.title: New Hire: Lucas Maes, Member of Technical Staff, Montreal
items.summary: PhD student at Mila focused on improving Joint Embedding Predictive Architectures (JEPAs) and world models through planning, temporal abstraction, goal specification, and physical reasoning.

items.title: New Research — LpWM: A Case for Sparse Representations in World Models
items.summary: AMI Labs’ new LpWorldModel (LpWM) research shows that making a JEPA world model’s internal representation sparse rather than dense can shift complexity out of the predictor, allowing simpler dynamics models to plan successfully while revealing more interpretable structure in how the world changes.

items.title: New Job Posting: AMI Scientist/Interns - Geometry and 3D Vision
items.summary: We believe that video is a rich and abundant source of data reflecting how the world works, and that in general models need to be able to process continuous, high-dimensional data from a variety of sensors to: (a) understand context about the current state of the physical world, (b) make predictions about how the world will evolve, possibly as a result of actions taken, and (c) plan and adapt sequences of actions to complete complex tasks, possibly in dynamic, complex environments.

newItems.title: Reconstruction or Semantics? What Makes a Latent Space Useful for Robotic World Models
newItems.tldr: This study advocates semantic latent space as a stronger foundation for policy-relevant robotics diffusion world models by comparing six reconstruction and semantic encoders to train world model variants under a fixed protocol on BridgeV2 dataset, and shows effective world model training in high-dimensional representation spaces with and without dimension compression.
newItems.abstract: World model-based policy evaluation is a practical proxy for testing real-world robot control by rolling out candidate actions in action-conditioned video diffusion models. As these models increasingly adopt latent diffusion modeling (LDM), choosing the right latent space becomes critical. While the status quo uses autoencoding latent spaces like VAEs that are primarily trained for pixel reconstruction, recent work suggests benefits from pretrained encoders with representation-aligned semantic latent spaces. We systematically evaluate these latent spaces for action-conditioned LDM by comparing.

newItems.title: TAPNext++: What's Next for Tracking Any Point (TAP)?
newItems.tldr: This work presents TAPNext++, a model that tracks points in sequences that are orders of magnitude longer while preserving the low memory and compute footprint of the architecture and demonstrates that recurrent transformers can be substantially improved for point tracking and set a new state-of-the-art on multiple benchmarks.
newItems.abstract: Tracking-Any-Point (TAP) models aim to track any point through a video, which is a crucial task in AR/XR and robotics applications. The recently introduced TAPNext approach proposes an end-to-end, recurrent transformer architecture to track points frame-by-frame in a purely online fashion -- demonstrating competitive performance at minimal latency. However, we show that TAPNext struggles with longer video sequences and also frequently fails to re-detect query points that reappear after being occluded or leaving the frame. In this work, we present TAPNext++, a model that tracks points in sequence.

newItems.title: Tapnext: Tracking Any Point (Tap) as Next Token Prediction
newItems.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
newItems.tldr: The TAPNext model is causal, tracks in a purely online fashion, and removes tracking-specific inductive biases, which enables TAPNext to run with minimal latency and removes the temporal windowing required by many existing state-of-the-art trackers.
newItems.abstract: Tracking Any Point (TAP) in a video is a challenging computer vision problem with many demonstrated applications in robotics, video editing, and 3D reconstruction. Existing TAP methods rely heavily on complex tracking-specific inductive biases and heuristics, limiting their generality and scalability. To address these challenges, we present TAPNext, a new approach that casts TAP as sequential masked token decoding. Our model is causal, tracks purely online, and removes tracking-specific inductive biases. This enables TAPNext to run with minimal latency.

newItems.title: TRecViT: A Recurrent Video Transformer
newItems.tldr: The proposed novel block, TRecViT, is causal and shows strong performance on sparse and dense tasks, trained in supervised or self-supervised regimes, being the first causal video model in the state-space models family.
newItems.abstract: We propose a novel block for \emph{causal} video modeling. It relies on a time-space-channel factorization with dedicated blocks for each dimension: gated linear recurrent units (LRUs) perform information mixing over time, self-attention layers perform mixing over space, and MLPs over channels. The resulting architecture \emph{TRecViT} is causal and shows strong performance on sparse and dense tasks, trained in supervised or self-supervised regimes, being the first causal video model in the state-space models family. Notably, our model outperforms or is on par with the popular (non-causal) Vi.

newItems.title: Unraveling the Complexity of Memory in RL Agents: an Approach for Classification and Evaluation
newItems.tldr: This paper provides practical, precise definitions of agent memory types, such as long-term vs. short-term memory and declarative vs. procedural memory, inspired by cognitive science, and proposes a robust experimental methodology for evaluating the memory capabilities of RL agents.

In particular, memory is paramount for tasks that require the use of past information, adaptation to novel environments, and improved sample efficiency. newItems.title: Interpretability in Action: Exploratory Analysis of VPT, a Minecraft Agent
newItems.tldr: This work performs exploratory analysis on the Video PreTraining (VPT) Minecraft playing agent, one of the largest open-source vision-based agents, and aims to illuminate its reasoning mechanisms by applying various interpretability techniques.
newItems.abstract: Understanding the mechanisms behind decisions taken by large foundation models in sequential decision-making tasks is critical to ensuring that such systems operate transparently and safely. In this work, we perform exploratory analysis on the Video PreTraining (VPT) Minecraft playing agent, one of the largest open-source vision-based agents. We aim to illuminate its reasoning mechanisms by applying various interpretability techniques. newItems.title: IDAT: A Multi-Modal Dataset and Toolkit for Building and Evaluating Interactive Task-Solving Agents
newItems.venue: Annual International ACM SIGIR Conference on Research and Development in Information Retrieval
newItems.tldr: A scalable data collection tool for gathering interactive grounded language instructions within a Minecraft-like environment, resulting in a Multi-Modal dataset and a Human-in-the-Loop interactive evaluation platform for qualitative analysis and comparison of agent performance through multi-turn communication with human annotators.
newItems.abstract: Seamless interaction between AI agents and humans using natural language remains a key goal in AI research. This paper addresses the challenges of developing interactive agents that can understand and execute grounded natural language instructions through the IGLU competition. Despite advancements, challenges such as a scarcity of appropriate datasets and the need for effective evaluation platforms persist. newItems.title: BindGPT: A Scalable Framework for 3D Molecular Design via Language Modeling and Reinforcement Learning
newItems.tldr: A novel generative model, BindGPT, which uses a conceptually simple but powerful approach to create 3D molecules within the protein's binding site, and shows how such a simple conceptual approach combined with pre-training and scaling can perform on par or better than the current best-specialized diffusion models, language models, and graph neural networks while being two orders of magnitude cheaper to sample.
newItems.abstract: Generating novel active molecules for a given protein is an extremely challenging task for generative models that requires an understanding of the complex physical interactions between the molecule and its environment. This paper presents a novel generative model, BindGPT, which uses a conceptually simple but powerful approach to create 3D molecules within the protein's binding site. Our model jointly produces molecular graphs and conformations, eliminating the need for an extra graph reconstruction step. newItems.tldr: This work integrates a new family of state space models (SSMs) in world models of MBRL agents to present a new method, Recall to Imagine (R2I), which aims to enhance both long-term memory and long-horizon credit assignment.

headline: AMI is building the scaffolding for causal world models
stateOfPlay: This week we highlight two papers, one new hire, one job posting, and a burst of evaluation-framework commits. Overall, they reveal a lab systematically attacking the same problem from multiple angles: how to build video representations that are not merely descriptive but causal, predictive, and cheap enough to scale. LeVJEPA strips JEPA-style video pretraining to its essentials and achieves up to 20.8× compute reduction versus V-JEPA 2; LpWM argues that sparse internal representations make world-model dynamics simpler and more interpretable; and the new Mila hire, Lucas Maes, the lead author on the LeWorldModel research paper, was recruited precisely for his work on planning and temporal abstraction inside JEPAs.

threads.title: LeVJEPA and LpWM together sketch AMI's architectural thesis: simpler is scalable
threads.narrative:
The release of the LeVJEPA and LpWM research papers addresses consecutive layers of the same problem. LeVJEPA — described by AMI as matching or beating V-JEPA 2 with as much as 20.8× less pretraining compute — achieves this by eliminating the target network, predictor, and stop-gradient that have become standard JEPA scaffolding. A single encoder, a single objective. The implication is architectural: AMI believes the complexity that earlier JEPA variants offloaded onto training heuristics can instead be absorbed into representation quality. Crucially, the paper also claims the resulting representations are causal — suited to future world models, not just frozen embeddings.

LpWM picks up exactly where LeVJEPA leaves off. If you want to build a planning system on top of video representations, what should those representations look like? AMI's answer, per the LpWorldModel paper, is sparse rather than dense. Sparsity shifts complexity out of the predictor — the dynamics model that forecasts how the world evolves — and yields more interpretable structure in how state changes. The two papers are complementary by design: one argues for simplicity in learning representations, the other argues for sparsity in using them for planning. Together they constitute something close to a design manifesto for AMI's world-model stack.

threads.title: Lucas Maes hire closes the loop from research to planning
threads.narrative:
AMI's recruitment of Lucas Maes, a Mila PhD student whose work centers on improving JEPAs through planning, temporal abstraction, goal specification, and physical reasoning, is not incidental to the research week. Maes was the lead author on LeWorldModel, a research paper co-authored with several other AMI Labs researchers and considered a breakthrough by making JEPA more stable. In that respect, his joining AMI seems somewhat inevitable. His first visible GitHub action was a comment on an issue in the galilai-group/stable-worldmodel repository, suggesting he is already engaging with world-model infrastructure.

The open Geometry and 3D Vision scientist/intern job posting in Paris adds a further dimension. Its job description frames video as the primary data source for understanding physical-world state, predicting how the world evolves, and planning action sequences — language that maps directly onto the three-capability agenda visible in LpWM and LeVJEPA. Hiring for 3D geometry suggests AMI intends to ground these video representations spatially, which would be a prerequisite for any robotics or embodied application of the world models the team is building.

threads.title: Brian Li's evaluation push signals AMI is preparing to benchmark its own models rigorously
threads.narrative:
Brian Li accounted for 15 of the week's 36 GitHub events, almost entirely concentrated in EvolvingLMMs-Lab/lmms-eval — a community evaluation framework for large multimodal models. He opened at least six pull requests and merged one that week. The volume and clustering of this activity suggests it is not routine maintenance but a structured effort to extend or adapt the eval suite, possibly to cover video or world-model outputs that AMI's own systems will need to be measured against.

This matters because AMI's research credibility depends on reproducible, externally legible benchmarking. LeVJEPA's headline claim — 20.8× compute savings against V-JEPA 2 — requires a trustworthy measurement apparatus. Li's sustained engagement with lmms-eval points to a team that is investing in the infrastructure of verification, not just in the models themselves.

evidence.label: Brian Li merged PR in lmms-eval

signals.text: Saining Xie publicly endorsed what he described as RAE extending to video, attracting 122 likes — a rare instance of a senior AMI figure amplifying external video-representation work in a week dominated by AMI's own video papers. It reinforces that the team is watching the broader field closely even as it publishes.

The bulk of the week's newly surfaced publications belong to Artem Zholus, whose prior work spans causal video transformers (TRecViT), point tracking (TAPNext, TAPNext++), and semantic latent spaces for robotic world models — a portfolio that aligns tightly with AMI's current agenda and suggests his research history was a significant factor in his recruitment.

whatToWatch: The convergence of LeVJEPA, LpWM, the Maes hire, and the 3D Vision opening suggests AMI continues to make progress on components such as efficient video pretraining, sparse world-model dynamics, planning expertise, and spatial grounding. How long it takes for this to be integrated into a single demonstrable system in terms of a unified world-model release or a robotics-adjacent benchmark result remains to be seen.
